findings.title: [P2] Compare file contents when checking probe isolation
findings.body: The main-tree integrity check compares only porcelain status entries, which contain paths and status codes rather than content hashes. If a tracked file was already modified before the probe, the probe can overwrite it through an absolute path while its entry remains ` M path`; the helper then exits successfully. Existing untracked files have the same problem. This lets executed probe code alter main-tree application files without triggering the promised failure. Snapshot and compare file contents, including existing dirty and untracked files, or enforce filesystem isolation during execution.

findings.description: chart-unblock-probe.sh is documented as 'the only way a decision:unblock ticket runs anything' and claims the probe 'never writes' to the main tree. The verdict is a before/after compare of `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` on MAIN. That check cannot see (a) the shared `.git` directory: a detached worktree shares `.git/config`, `.git/hooks`, refs and objects with the main repo, so `git config core.hooksPath`/`core.fsmonitor`/`core.pager`, dropping a `.git/hooks/post-checkout`, pushing or rewriting branches all succeed and leave status unchanged; (b) any path outside the repository (`~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.bashrc`, other checkouts); (c) new files inside an already-ignored directory, because `--ignored=matching` lists only the matching directory entry, not its contents; (d) edits to tracked files that were already dirty before the probe. The probe argv is arbitrary and runs with the operator's full privileges and no filesystem isolation.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock ticket probe (or a prompt-injected agent crafting one) plants a git hook or `core.fsmonitor` in the shared `.git`, or writes to the home directory; the helper exits 0 reporting 'main tree unchanged', and the payload executes on the operator's next git command in the main repo.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not treat the status compare as the boundary. Run the probe in a clone (`git clone --shared` or `git worktree` with `GIT_DIR` of a throwaway copy of `.git`), set `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `HOME=$SCRATCH`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, and compare a hash of `.git/config` and `.git/hooks` plus `git for-each-ref` before/after. Use `--ignored=traditional` so files inside ignored directories are enumerated. Document that out-of-repo writes are not detected.

findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/commands/chart.md states the sole unattended exception is `close <slug> --consumed-by <cycle>` 'on a handed-off map', and .claude/scripts/chart-guard.sh --close-consumed admits any unattended context; op_close is the only place the map's Status could be checked and it does not.
findings.description: `op_close --consumed-by` skips the interactive-context check (correct per design) but never verifies that the map's `**Status**` is `handed-off`. It then rejects every open ledger row (`dw reject ... map closed: consumed by ...`), closes every bead and the epic, and sets Status `closed`. `--consumed-by` only has to match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; no cycle id is validated against anything. chart-guard.sh --close-consumed likewise lets any unattended context through. Combined, an unattended agent (autonomous run, LOA_UNATTENDED=1) can close a map that is still `charting`, disposing of the operator's open decisions. This is exactly the write path the 'interactive only' invariant exists to prevent.
findings.failure_mode: During an autonomous /plan-and-analyze, the agent runs `chart-ticket.sh close --map <slug> --consumed-by <anything>` on a charting map; all open decision rows become `rejected` by `chart`, beads and epic are closed, and the PRD proceeds as if the map were settled.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_close, when `--consumed-by` is given require `doc_field Status == handed-off` (and that a snapshot `grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md` exists) before any write; die otherwise. Have chart-guard.sh --close-consumed accept a `--map` and perform the same Status check. Consider validating `--consumed-by` against the sprint ledger's cycle ids.

findings.cross_file_justification: agent-types.yaml newly registers chart-researcher as write_capable: true; the diff hunk of chart-researcher.md grants `Write`; chart-ticket.sh op_research_end is the only compensating control and has the blind spots in SEC-4. Note: the P0 full-file copy of chart-researcher.md shows `tools: [Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch]` with no Write, conflicting with the diff hunk and with agent-types.yaml; the two must be reconciled.
findings.description: The diff's chart-researcher frontmatter grants `Write` alongside `WebFetch`, and agent-types.yaml marks the agent `write_capable: true`. The only restriction on what it writes ('exactly one file ... no other Write call, under any path') is prose in the system prompt. The agent fetches arbitrary web pages, which it is told to treat as data, but a prompt-injected page can direct it to write anywhere the Write tool is allowed (e.g. `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings.json`, `~/.claude/`). The post-hoc check in `op_research_end` only inspects `git status` of the repo and exempts the whole `grimoires/loa/research/` tree, so out-of-repo writes, writes into ignored directories, and overwrites of other tickets' reports or dispatch markers pass. The P0 full file removes Write, which would resolve this, but agent-types.yaml still declares the agent write-capable and the diff hunk still grants Write.
findings.failure_mode: A fetched page contains instructions; the researcher writes a hook, settings file, or a second 'report' with injected content under grimoires/loa/research/; research-end passes; the charting session inlines the report into the hand-off snapshot that /plan-and-analyze reads as priority-1 context.
findings.suggested_fix: Ship the no-Write variant (final message returned to the session, which saves it) and set agent-types.yaml `chart-researcher: write_capable: false`. If Write must remain, restrict it by path in the agent's tool permissions, not prose, and make research-end fail on any status delta except the single expected report path.

findings.description: The research scope check is a one-directional set difference (`comm -13`) of `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` lines taken before and after the subagent, with every path under `grimoires/loa/research/` excluded. Blind spots: (1) a tracked file already modified before dispatch keeps its ` M path` line, so further edits are invisible; (2) `--ignored=matching` lists an ignored directory as one `!! dir/` entry, so new files inside ignored directories are not enumerated (only `.run` and `.beads` get a separate `find -newer`, capped at 20 entries); (3) lines that disappear (deleting an untracked file, reverting a change) are not reported because only additions are compared; (4) anything written outside the repository root; (5) any write under grimoires/loa/research/, including other tickets' reports and the `.chart-<slug>-*.dispatch` markers that enforce the 5-dispatch cap (a subagent can delete markers to reset the cap, or replace the marker with a symlink so the next `research-begin` `printf > "$m"` follows it).
findings.failure_mode: A subagent with Write modifies an already-dirty tracked file or drops a file into an ignored directory; research-end reports no change and the ticket is accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare content hashes (`git diff --no-index` against a recorded tree, or `git stash create`/`git write-tree` before and after plus hashes of untracked and ignored files via `--ignored=traditional`), use a symmetric diff, narrow the exemption to the single expected report path, and store dispatch markers outside the directory the subagent may write (e.g. under `.run/`).

findings.description: FR-1.1 now lets `git branch -D spike/<slug>` through when `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` contains a row with `status: decided`, `source: grimoires/loa/spikes/<slug>.md`, and a `→ decided` transition whose `by` starts with `operator:`. The ledger is a plain tracked YAML file that the same agent the hook is guarding can edit with its Write/Edit tools; nothing in the check verifies that the row was written by dec-write-lib.sh or by a human (no signature, no cross-check against git authorship). The `operator:` prefix is just a string. The safety hook therefore delegates its decision to data under the control of the party it restricts.
findings.failure_mode: The agent appends a synthetic decided row with `by: operator:x` to decisions.yaml, then runs `git branch -D spike/<slug>` and the hook allows it, deleting unmerged (and possibly unpushed) prototype work.
findings.suggested_fix: Require corroboration the agent cannot forge: e.g. the ledger row must be committed (`git log -1 -- grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` not dirty, `git diff --quiet HEAD -- grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`), the spike branch must be present on `origin/spike/<slug>` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor spike/<slug> origin/spike/<slug>` must hold, or route deletions through the sanctioned prune helper which can take the same evidence.

findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh op_handoff is the intended writer of grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md, but plan-and-analyze.md and plan.md trust any file matching that glob as 'settled decisions; confirm, do not re-ask' without tying it to a map doc with Status handed-off or to ledger rows.
findings.description: The hand-off snapshot glob `grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md` is promoted to priority-1 context with the instruction that its decisions are 'settled, so confirm them in the interview and do not re-ask them', and the unattended path consumes it without an operator. Nothing checks that a matching `grimoires/loa/maps/<slug>.md` exists with Status `handed-off`, that the referenced ledger rows exist, or that the snapshot was produced by op_handoff. A file dropped in that directory by any contributor (PR, merge, or a Write-capable subagent) becomes authoritative requirements that the agent is told not to question. Previously, `context/*.md` was priority 2 'user-provided context'.
findings.failure_mode: A planted `context/chart-foo.md` with fabricated 'settled' decisions is ingested as priority-1 and reproduced in the PRD in an autonomous run without being re-asked.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the planning skill accept a snapshot only when `maps/<slug>.md` exists with `**Status**: handed-off` and the ledger has `source: map:<slug>/*` rows; otherwise treat the file as ordinary priority-2 context. Consider having op_handoff record a content hash of the snapshot in the map doc and verifying it on ingestion.

findings.description:
`section_append` passes the new bullet via `awk -v line="$2"`. awk processes backslash escapes in `-v` assignments, so a value containing `
` (two characters) becomes a real newline in the output. `san1` strips control characters and URLs but not backslashes, so `--line 'ok
## Out of scope
- injected'` or a `--why`/`--name` value can inject new headings, bullets, or a second `**Status**:` line into the tracked map doc. The map doc is later inlined verbatim (headings demoted) into the hand-off snapshot that /plan-and-analyze treats as settled context.
findings.failure_mode: Structure of the map doc is corrupted or extra 'decisions' appear in the snapshot without a ledger row.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the line through the environment (`line="$2" awk '... ENVIRON["line"] ...'`) or via `printf '%s' | awk` on a separate stream; alternatively strip backslashes in san1.

findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/scripts/chart-frontier.sh and chart-ticket.sh bead_row accept either `.issue_type` or `.type` from br JSON, while get-ready-work.sh filters only on `.issue_type`; a br build emitting `type` would let question beads through the build path that implement.md and implementing-tasks/SKILL.md now rely on this script to exclude.
findings.description: The question-bead exclusion that the build path now depends on (`/implement` was changed to call this script instead of `br ready`) keys only on `.issue_type`. Sibling scripts in the same change defensively read `.issue_type // .type`, acknowledging that br releases differ. If br reports `type`, every decision ticket passes the filter and becomes selectable build work, silently defeating the 'tickets cannot enter a sprint' guarantee.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous /run picks up a `question` bead as a task and starts implementing a decision that was never made.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `((.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase) != "question"` consistently, and add a test with the `type` key shape.

findings.description: SP-1 is explicitly a fence and documents several misses, but a few cheap, undocumented bypasses exist that move spike content into another branch: `git fetch origin spike/x && git merge FETCH_HEAD` (fetch is unguarded; the merge names no spike ref), `git merge -` after `git checkout spike/x` then `git checkout main`, `git format-patch main..spike/x | git am` (format-patch unguarded), `git read-tree -u spike/x`, and `git checkout spike/x -- .` in a separate invocation after `cd`. The `gh pr create` no-head check also runs `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` in the hook's cwd rather than the command's `-C`/`cd` target.
findings.failure_mode: Spike content is merged or opened as a PR despite the fence, undetected by the hook and only caught by review.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `fetch` of a spike ref to the blocked verbs when followed by `merge FETCH_HEAD` in the same command, block `git merge -`, `read-tree`, and `format-patch` naming spike refs, and extend the documented misses list; consider a server-side branch protection rule rejecting merges whose second parent is a spike/* head.
